sourcedFrom: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 (2021)
cleanIntro: FN America's High Power: an exposed-hammer, single-action 9mm with a manual safety, stripped by rotating the takedown lever 90 degrees counterclockwise and running the slide off the front. Before any of that, this guide has one job — making sure the pistol in your hand is the FN America gun this book describes and not a legacy Herstal or Browning Hi Power, which is a different design with a different takedown.

steps.title: Is this an FN America High Power, or a legacy Hi Power?
steps.action: Read the markings on the slide and frame. This procedure applies only to the FN High Power produced by FN America, LLC. If your pistol is an older High Power or Hi Power from FN Herstal, Browning Arms Company or anyone else, stop here — those pistols are designed differently and function differently.
steps.prose: This is the single most consequential restriction in FN's entire catalogue of manuals, because "High Power" is a name shared by seventy years of pistols that are not this one. The legacy guns have a different takedown, different internals and, on many of them, a magazine disconnect and a different safety arrangement. FN's own answer if you are unsure is to phone Customer Service on 1-800-635-1321 before proceeding further — and that is the right move, because guessing here means applying the wrong disassembly to a pistol that will not do it.
steps.aside: The book's page-2 scope line: IF YOUR FN PISTOL DOES NOT HAVE FN HIGH POWER™ IN ITS NAMING CONVENTION OR IF THE APPEARANCE OF THE PISTOL DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO THE ILLUSTRATIONS IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL CONTACT YOUR DEALER, DEPARTMENT ARMORER OR CONTACT FN DIRECTLY TO OBTAIN THE OWNER’S MANUAL THAT HAS BEEN WRITTEN SPECIFICALLY FOR YOUR PISTOL.
steps.quote: The FN High Power described in this manual refers only and specifically to the pistol produced by FN America, LLC. Legacy “High Power” or “Hi Power” pistols made by FN Herstal S.A., Browning Arms Company, or any other manufacturer are designed and will function differently.
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §4 Dry firing & dummy rounds, p.15
steps.warn: If you are unsure what type or model of pistol you own, please call FN Customer Service at 1-800-635-1321 before proceeding further.

steps.title: Check what has been through it: +P yes, +P+ never
steps.action: Before you clean, know what this pistol has been fed. The FN High Power is designed to function safely and reliably with +P ammunition. It must never be fired with +P+, or with ammunition intended for submachine guns or rifles.
steps.prose: This matters at the bench, not just at the range: +P+ does not conform to SAAMI or CIP guidelines and can develop chamber pressures above industry standards, and a pistol that has been fed it deserves a careful look at the locking lugs and the breech face while it is apart. The caliber is marked on the rear of the barrel and visible through the ejection port, so you can confirm the chambering with the slide locked back in a moment. If anything looks battered or peened during this clean, that history is the first thing to ask about.
steps.aside: FN's positive statement in the same section: THE FN HIGH POWER IS DESIGNED TO SAFELY AND RELIABLY FUNCTION WITH +P AMMUNITION.
steps.quote: DO NOT USE +P+ AMMUNITION IN THE FN HIGH POWER AS IT COULD RESULT IN SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH.
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §3 Ammunition, p.11

steps.title: Magazine out, and pull it if the well is dirty
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, safety engaged. Press the magazine release and take the magazine out; if it does not drop free, pull on the base plate while holding the release in.
steps.prose: Magazine before chamber, always — with a loaded magazine still seated, racking the slide chambers a round instead of clearing one, and FN says so in the warning at the head of this section. The High Power's magazine sits in a steel-framed well that collects grit rather than shedding it, so a sticky magazine is common on a pistol that has not been cleaned lately. Take it right out and put it down away from the work.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. If the magazine does not drop out of the pistol, pull on the magazine base plate while pressing the magazine release (Figure 12).
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §6.3 Unloading, step 1, p.22

steps.title: Rack, lock the slide open, and look
steps.action: Pull the slide back to eject any chambered round, press the slide stop up so the slide rests open against it, then look into the chamber and down the magazine well and confirm both are empty.
steps.prose: The slide stop is ambidextrous on this pistol, so either thumb can hold it up while the other hand eases the slide back onto it. The High Power is single action with an exposed hammer, which means the hammer is now cocked and stays that way through the strip — a useful visual confirmation you have not accidentally dropped it. Removing the magazine tells you nothing about the chamber; the look is what does.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and magazine well to ensure no cartridge is present. Remember, merely removing the magazine does not mean the chamber is unloaded (Figure 14).
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §6.3 Unloading, step 3, p.22

steps.title: Understand the safety before you handle a cocked hammer
steps.action: Note where the safety levers sit at the rear of the frame and how they behave. Up is engaged, blocking the sear; down exposes a red dot and frees the mechanism. It cannot be engaged with the hammer down, so do not force it there.
steps.prose: The High Power is cocked-and-locked by design, and FN's warnings around it are worth reading before, not after: forcing the safety lever with the hammer down can damage the safety mechanism and require repair before the pistol is used again. There is a second, blunter warning too — never lower the hammer by hand with a cartridge chambered, because pulling the trigger to release it disengages the safety mechanisms. Since the chamber has just been confirmed empty, none of that applies right now, which is exactly why the sequence runs in this order.
steps.quote: NOTICE! THE SAFETY OF THE FN HIGH POWER CANNOT BE ENGAGED WHEN THE HAMMER IS IN THE FIRED (DOWN/ FORWARD) POSITION.
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §9.2 Manual safety, p.29
steps.warn: THE MANUAL SAFETY CAN NOT BE ENGAGED WITH THE HAMMER IN THE DOWN/FORWARD POSITION. FORCING THE SAFETY LEVER CAN DAMAGE THE SAFETY MECHANISM REQUIRING REPAIR OF THE PISTOL BEFORE CONTINUED USE!

steps.title: Start from a confirmed-empty pistol with the slide locked back
steps.action: Re-confirm the chamber and magazine well are empty, then retract the slide and lock it in its rearward position on the slide stop.
steps.prose: FN opens the field strip by pointing back at the unloading section and then immediately asking for the slide locked open, because the takedown lever cannot rotate against a closed slide. Get it fully back and properly on the stop — a slide that slips off partway through the next step comes forward under a live recoil spring with your fingers near the muzzle. FN also recommends the safety be disengaged for disassembly, so put it down now.
steps.quote: Completely unload the pistol as described in Section 6.3 and remove the magazine. Inspect the chamber and the magazine well to verify that the pistol is completely unloaded (Figure 31).
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.1 Field strip, step 1, p.34

steps.title: Takedown lever 90 degrees COUNTERclockwise
steps.action: With the slide locked open, rotate the takedown lever approximately 90 degrees counterclockwise until it stops.
steps.prose: Counterclockwise, and only ninety degrees — this is the one FN pistol in the range that turns the other way, against the 509's 100 degrees clockwise and the 502's 108. Habit from another FN is the commonest reason a High Power lever feels stuck, because the owner is turning it the wrong way against its stop. Keep the slide locked back while you turn; if the lever will not move, check the slide has not crept forward before applying any more thumb.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever approximately 90° counterclockwise (Figure 33).
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.1 Field strip, step 3, p.34

steps.title: Release the slide and ease it forward
steps.action: Take a firm grip on the slide, release it off the slide stop and let it move forward under control rather than letting it snap shut.
steps.prose: The next movement runs straight on into taking the slide off the frame, so a controlled release saves re-establishing your grip on a spring-loaded assembly. There is no trigger press anywhere in the High Power strip — the hammer stays cocked throughout, which is one of the practical differences between this pistol and the striker-fired FN 509. Keep your support hand behind the muzzle, not in front of it.
steps.quote: While holding the slide with one hand, release the slide from the slide stop and ease it forward (Figure 34).
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.1 Field strip, step 4, p.34

steps.title: Slide forward and off the frame — mind the recoil spring
steps.action: Pull the slide forward off the frame rails and lift it away. Position your hand to catch the recoil spring and guide: they are under tension and are not captive in the assembled position.
steps.prose: This is where the High Power differs most from FN's polymer pistols. The recoil spring and its guide are under spring tension in the assembled pistol and FN puts a note in the middle of the strip telling you to have a hand ready for them — they can and will jump out as the slide separates. Cup your palm around the front underside of the slide as it comes off and nothing goes anywhere. Once it is clear, everything relaxes.
steps.quote: Remove the slide by pulling the slide forward and away from the frame (Figure 35).
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.1 Field strip, step 5, p.34
steps.warn: Note: The recoil spring and recoil spring guide are under spring tension. Ensure that your hand is positioned to capture the spring and guide when they are removed from the assembled position.

steps.title: Recoil spring guide out from behind, rear end first
steps.action: Hold the slide upside down. Take hold of the recoil spring guide with your hand positioned behind it, then lift the rear of the guide and its spring up and out of the slide.
steps.prose: Behind the guide, not on top of it — that hand position is what keeps the spring from launching when the rear end comes free. The High Power's spring and guide are two separate items rather than a captive assembly, so they will part company happily; keep them together on the bench in the order they came out. Lifting from the rear releases the load instead of fighting it.
steps.quote: Hold the slide upside down, grasp the recoil spring guide, with the hand positioned behind the guide, and lift the rear of the recoil spring guide and recoil spring up and out of the slide (Figure 36).
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.1 Field strip, step 6, p.35

steps.title: Barrel up, forward around the extractor, then back and out
steps.action: Grip the barrel by its lug, lift it up and forward around the extractor, then slide it rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Four movements packed into one instruction and the forward part is the one people miss — up, forward to clear, around the extractor, then rearward out. On the High Power the barrel is a tilting, locking barrel, so the lug has to clear its seat before anything else can happen. Forcing it straight back with the lug still down drives the barrel hood into the extractor claw, which is a sprung part you do not want to reset. That completes the strip.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel by its lug, lift it up and forward around the extractor then slide the barrel rearward out of the slide (Figure 37)
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.1 Field strip, step 7, p.36

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame with the hammer cocked, slide, barrel, recoil spring and recoil spring guide on the bench. That is FN's field strip level for this pistol; the grips, backstraps and magazine come apart in the deeper procedures.
steps.prose: From here the bore and chamber are reachable from the breech end, along with the breech face, the extractor, the barrel's locking lugs and unlock surface, the slide rails and the magazine well. Check the locking lugs and breech face carefully if this pistol has seen a lot of hot ammunition — the +P+ prohibition earlier exists because pressure damage shows up in those two places first. The grips, the upper and lower backstraps and the magazine are what Deep Clean covers.
steps.quote: The FN High Power uses an exposed hammer, single action mechanism with a manual safety to fire the pistol.
steps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §8 Function of the FN High Power, p.27

deepSteps.title: Grips off with a properly fitting screwdriver
deepSteps.action: Fit a standard slotted screwdriver that closely matches the grip screw slot. Rotate the screw counterclockwise until it is free; if the grip does not fall away, put a finger inside the magazine well and press outward to free it. Repeat for the other side. Each grip is held by one screw and located by features in the frame.
deepSteps.prose: The screwdriver fit is the whole instruction — a blade that is too narrow or too thin cams out and chews the screw slot, and grip screws are the most visible fastener on the pistol. Pressing outward from inside the magazine well is FN's own trick for a grip that has stuck to the frame, and it works far better than prising at the edges. Going back on, the grip should sit flat against the frame before the screw is started; if it does not, shift it until the frame's locating features engage.
deepSteps.caution: Do not overtighten the grip screw. Overtightening may damage the grip and cause it to pull away from the frame at the top and bottom.
deepSteps.quote: Align the screwdriver with the grip screw and rotate the screw counterclockwise until it is free (Figure 46).
deepSteps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.3.1 Removing the grips, p.39

deepSteps.title: Backstraps off — and the hammer spring is behind them
deepSteps.action: With the pistol stripped and empty, depress the backstrap latch with a punch, small screwdriver or similar tool and slide the lower backstrap down and off the frame. Then slide the upper backstrap down and off. Stop there: do not attempt to remove the hammer spring.
deepSteps.prose: Taking the backstraps off exposes the hammer spring, which is under tension and held in by the orange hammer spring retainer — and FN's warning is unambiguous that removing it is not recommended without training, because an unintentionally released retainer and spring can be thrown from the pistol with great force. The orange colour is there to make it obvious what you are looking at. Clean around it, not into it: the backstrap channel is the point of this job.
deepSteps.quote: Using a punch, small screwdriver or similar tool depress the backstrap latch and slide the lower back strap down and off the frame (Figure 51).
deepSteps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §11.4.1 Upper and lower backstrap removal, step 1, p.40
deepSteps.warn: CAUTON: REMOVING THE HAMMER SPRING IS NOT RECOMMENDED WITHOUT TRAINING. IF UNINTENTIONALLY RELEASED THE RETAINER AND HAMMER SPRING CAN BE THROWN FROM THE PISTOL WITH GREAT FORCE RESULTING IN THE LOSS OF PARTS OR SERIOUS INJURY.

deepSteps.title: Dry firing this pistol: occasional and for disassembly, not for practice
deepSteps.action: Do not use the High Power for routine dry-fire practice. Occasional dry firing, and dry firing as part of disassembly, is acceptable; for regular practice use snap caps.
deepSteps.prose: FN says regular dry firing may damage the striker on this pistol — worth noting because the High Power is an exposed-hammer gun and the wording still points at the firing-pin assembly as the part that suffers. It also warns that dummy rounds with empty primer pockets are fine for loading and unloading drills but do not protect the striker during dry firing, which is a distinction people routinely miss. If this pistol has been dry-fired hard, inspect the firing pin tip and the breech face while everything is apart.
deepSteps.quote: Occasional dry firing of your FN High Power and for disassembly is acceptable.
deepSteps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §4 Dry firing & dummy rounds, p.13

deepSteps.title: Read the caliber off the barrel while it is out
deepSteps.action: With the barrel out of the slide, read the caliber marking on its rear face — the same marking you would normally see through the ejection port — and confirm it against the ammunition you have been using.
deepSteps.prose: It is a thirty-second check and it is the one that closes out the ammunition question from the start of this walk. On a legacy-name pistol like this, where owners often inherit magazines and ammunition along with the gun, it is worth doing once properly rather than assuming. Look at the locking lugs on the same face while you are there: peening or bright wear on the lugs is what over-pressure ammunition leaves behind.
deepSteps.quote: The caliber of the FN High Power is located on the rear of the barrel and is visible through the ejection port.
deepSteps.cite: FN HIGH POWER™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2106-FN HIGH POWER-OM 66-100701 — §2 Basic safety rules, rule 8, p.9

cleaning.name: BARREL, BORE & LOCKING LUGS
tasks: Solvent into the bore and chamber, a few minutes to work, then rod and patches from the chamber end only
Keep the rod off the crown; damage to the muzzle affects accuracy
Patch until they come out clean, then a patch moistened with preservative oil through the bore for protection
Brush and inspect the locking lugs and the barrel's unlock surface — that is where pressure and wear show first
Light film of gun oil on the outside of the barrel

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & FRAME
tasks: Brush and solvent on the breech face, under the extractor and around the ejection port
Wipe the slide rails both sides and lubricate them lightly with lightweight gun oil
Clean and lightly oil the recoil spring guide and spring; keep them as a pair
Soft cloth into the steel magazine well to lift grit; if the grips are off, clean the frame flats underneath them
Check the disassembled parts for wear or damage while they are apart, and ask FN about anything doubtful rather than reassembling it

cleaning.name: INTERVAL & PUT-AWAY
tasks: Never soak the pistol in solvent or lubricant, and keep oil sparing — excess interferes with function
Clean and lubricate after every use; a light coat of preservative oil on the metal increases corrosion resistance on a steel-framed pistol
Wipe the exterior down to remove dirt, fingerprints and excess lubricant before storage
Dry-patch the bore before shooting so storage oil is not in front of the first round
Store with the chamber and magazine empty; the safety cannot be engaged with the hammer down, so do not force it

reassembly: Barrel into the slide first: muzzle out through the barrel hole from the inside, dropped down, then slid back to the breech face until the lug locks.

Recoil spring onto the recoil spring guide, then the spring placed against the recess in the front of the slide, compressed with the guide, and the back of the guide seated centred on the front of the barrel lug.
Takedown lever must be in the down position before the slide assembly will go onto the frame — FN states this explicitly.
Guide the slide and barrel onto the frame, run the slide fully rearward and lock it on the slide stop.
Rotate the takedown lever upward to lock frame and slide together, then release the slide forward.
Test the slide stop, trigger, magazine release and manual safety with the pistol empty before anything is loaded.
If the grips came off: grip flat on the frame, screw started by hand and tightened with thumb and index finger only — never overtightened.
fncheck: Empty and reassembled: the takedown lever should sit flush and refuse to rotate against a closed slide; the slide should run fully into battery under its own spring and lock back on either ambidextrous stop; the hammer should cock as the slide is cycled and stay cocked; with the hammer cocked the safety levers should snap up into engagement on their detent and block the trigger, and drop back down to expose the red dot — and they should refuse to engage with the hammer down, which is correct behaviour and not a fault; and an empty magazine should seat and drop free when the release is pressed.
